expectations.text: Output has a valid SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter containing name and description
expectations.evidence: No SKILL.md was produced at all — output is weekly_digest.py, a standalone Python CLI script, plus .env.example, sample_data/, and a shell wrapper.

expectations.text: Names HubSpot and Slack as connectors by name only — no API keys, tokens, or credential values anywhere in the output
expectations.evidence: No credential VALUES leaked (pass on that narrow point), but the design uses raw API tokens read from .env (HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN, SLACK_BOT_TOKEN) rather than platform connectors — the assertion's premise (a skill naming connectors) doesn't apply since no skill artifact exists.
run_weekly_digest.sh is framed as a cron/launchd wrapper for scheduled Monday runs; RUN_NOTES.md assumes a Mon-Sun week.

expectations.text: States an explicit success bar distinguishing a good run from a technically-complete one
expectations.evidence: No equivalent 'good vs technically complete' framing exists anywhere in the script, comments, or RUN_NOTES.md.

expectations.text: Names at least one concrete failure mode (e.g. missing RevOps Slack post, HubSpot auth failure, zero closed-won deals)
expectations.evidence: Script implements 4 cross-reference buckets including 'in-HubSpot-but-not-mentioned' and an 'unparseable line' fallback; defaults to draft-only unless --post is passed.

expectations.text: Includes a delegation plan (primary vs. sub-agent execution per step)
expectations.evidence: No delegation concept — it's a single monolithic script with no sub-agent/model-routing plan.
